name: Dumbbell Renegade Row
summary: A row performed from a push-up plank position on two dumbbells. It trains the back while the trunk fights to resist rotation, making it a strong core and back combination.
setup: Place two hex or fixed dumbbells on the floor, shoulder-width apart, so they cannot roll.
Get into a push-up position with your hands gripping the dumbbells and feet wider than hip-width for balance.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
execution: Shift your weight slightly onto the left hand and row the right dumbbell toward your lower ribs.
Keep your hips level and square to the floor while you row.
Lower the dumbbell back to the floor with control.
Repeat on the other side, alternating, and rest the dumbbell fully before changing sides.
cues: Pull the elbow to the hip
mistakes: Twisting the hips as you row: widen your feet and brace harder, or kneel to regress.
Sagging in the lower back: squeeze the glutes and keep ribs down.
Using round dumbbells that roll: use hex or fixed dumbbells, or switch to hands on a stable platform.
Using too much weight: pick light dumbbells so every rep keeps the plank solid.
